problems.problem: Spread, raised by the first critic and not taken up by the revisions: Rāmānuja still holds 11 of 18 days (1, 5 to 12, 14, 16) and Madhva only 17 and 18, and the gate still warns on it. Day 12 is the clearest place where another commentator has a real, school-marking comment on the key verse: Śaṅkara (Mahadeva Sastri, on 12.5) takes those set on the Unmanifest as those who identify themselves with the Imperishable and contemplate the Supreme Reality, their greater trouble being the need to abandon attachment to the body, while Rāmānuja takes the Unmanifested as the individual soul; Madhva (Subba Rau, on 12.5) takes it as Avyakta worshipped as separated from the Lord, a path of great pains because without Devi’s grace there is no grace of the Lord. The two schools genuinely differ on this line and the batch names only one.
problems.fix: Keep the plain sense and name two: ...; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 12.5, reads the Unmanifested as the Imperishable Supreme Reality, hard to reach because attachment to the body must be abandoned, and Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 12.5, as the individual soul (by: shankara, by2: ramanuja, 60 words at most, src naming both editions). Or, as well, give day 14 to Madhva (Dvaita), on 14.26, from the Subba Rau paragraph in the packet (Brahman here the intelligent Prakriti; to become fit is to be as beloved of the Lord as she is), keeping the revised plain sense.
